event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: COVID-19 is portrayed by Colgate-Palmolive (CL) as a recent, multi-dimensional threat that has already disrupted – and may still disrupt – virtually every pillar of its global value chain.  The company discloses both realised impacts (e.g., supply-chain interruptions in China and travel-retail, on-line demand shifts, stay-at-home orders) and forward-looking exposures (labour shortages, raw-material scarcity, logistics bottlenecks, capital-market volatility, regulatory restrictions).  Language is mostly specific (naming concrete channels, functions and geographies) and links the pandemic to material outcomes such as sales volatility, additional production costs, and possible plant closures.  Because the filing date (16-Feb-2023) is less than three years after the WHO declaration (11-Mar-2020), the Time-Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  Mitigating language is minimal (“largely abated,” “we continue to monitor”), so the overall risk profile remains elevated.  Accordingly, the evidence sentences cluster in the upper range (6-9/10), reflecting recent timing, direct operational impact and breadth of exposure.

evidence_list.snippet: We face various risks related to pandemics, epidemics or similar widespread public health concerns, including the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicitly identifies COVID-19 as a risk category.
Forward-looking wording ('face various risks') indicates continuing exposure.
Statement is generic and unquantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sets the risk context but offers no specifics or quantified impact, yielding a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: • disruptions to our global supply chain, including the closure of manufacturing and distribution facilities, due to, among other things, the lack of availability of raw and packaging materials or manufacturing components; a decrease in our workforce or in the efficiency of such workforce, including as a result of illness, travel restrictions, absenteeism or governmental regulations; transportation and logistics challenges, including as a result of port and border closures and other governmental restrictions or volume and capacity restraints; or the impact of a pandemic, epidemic or other health emergencies, such as the COVID-19 pandemic on our retailers, third party suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers or distributors;

components.reason: Details multiple direct operational impacts (plant closures, raw-material shortages, logistics bottlenecks).
Adds labour-force degradation element (illness, absenteeism).
Links each impact explicitly to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly granular list of COVID-driven supply-chain and labour disruptions produces a near-maximum score.

evidence_list.snippet: • volatility in the demand for and availability of our products, which may be caused by the temporary inability of our consumers to purchase our products due to illness, financial hardship, quarantine, government actions mandating the closure of our facilities, distributors or retailers and/or imposing travel or movement restrictions, shifts in demand and consumption away from more discretionary or higher priced products to lower-priced products or pantry-loading activity;

components.reason: Addresses demand-side shocks and channel closures attributable to pandemic measures.
Specifies consumer behaviour shifts (down-trading, pantry-loading).
Forward-looking conditional language (‘may be caused’) reduces certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures material consumer-demand volatility but remains hypothetical, yielding a mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: • changes in purchasing patterns of our consumers, including a shift to purchasing our products online and disruptions in certain channels;

components.reason: Identifies structural channel shift (e-commerce) induced by pandemic.
Mentions channel disruption without quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights lasting demand-channel changes; limited depth keeps severity moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic, many of the communities in which we manufacture, market and sell our products experienced and may in the future experience “stay at home” orders, travel or movement restrictions and other government actions to address the pandemic.

components.reason: States that government lockdowns have already affected manufacturing and sales locations.
Explicitly allows for future recurrence (‘may in the future experience’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates realised operational hindrance and future risk, producing an elevated score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also experienced and may continue to experience certain disruptions to our global supply chain due to COVID-19, which have impacted and may continue to impact sales of and consumer access to our products.

components.reason: Admits past and ongoing supply-chain disruptions directly tied to COVID-19.
Links disruptions to concrete outcomes—reduced sales and consumer access.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past impact plus ongoing exposure with sales effect justifies a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: While the impact of COVID-19 on our business has largely abated at this time, uncertainties continue, particularly in China where we have substantial manufacturing facilities and business, and in the travel retail channel, where we have experienced and may continue to experience disruptions particularly in our Filorga business.

components.reason: Acknowledges geographic and channel-specific disruptions persisting (China, travel retail).
Notes partial abatement, signalling mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Contains both mitigation and ongoing risk; net effect is a modest but relevant score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also witnessed and may continue to witness changes in the purchasing patterns of our customers, including a shift in many markets to purchasing our products online.

components.reason: Confirms observed and continuing demand-channel shift triggered by pandemic behaviour.
No immediate negative financial quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Evidence of enduring consumer shift; limited detail keeps score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 may continue to impact consumer behavior and preferences, shopping patterns and consumption preferences.

components.reason: Highlights forward-looking uncertainty over demand fundamentals.
Highly generic—no operational or financial specifics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic forecast warrants a low-to-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: • political or economic instability, geopolitical events, wars and military conflicts, such as the war in Ukraine, environmental events, widespread health emergencies, such as COVID-19 or other pandemics or epidemics, natural disasters or social or labor unrest;

components.reason: Lists COVID-19 among destabilising global factors.
Broad, catch-all language dilutes precision.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Very generic placement of COVID-19 among many risks; per Time-Decay still relevant but minimal severity.
